To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the process of adaptation to school after entry is characterized by a rapid decline in the intensity of security seeking and inhibition, which is more marked in regular classes than in special classes, that the decline in intensity of these behaviors is more marked in boys than in girls, that the intensity of these behaviors at school entry is positively related to the intensity of family stress, and that the intensity of security-seeking and inhibition at school entry is predictive of internalizing behavior problems by the end of the first three months at school

(1) children from special classes score higher than children from regular kindergartens on the Security Seeking scale and more variable on both scales; (2) girls score higher on both scales than boys; and (3) initial high scores on both scales predict the development of internalized behavior problems in the special class, especially for girls.
the emotional security-seeking behavior of young children is a major determinant of their adaptation after entry to kindergarten.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how young children adapt to school after entry.
the development of emotional security after school entry.
early adaptation after children enter school, and the way this process can be understood by means of security-seeking and behavioral inhibition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more a child is inhibited and security seeking, the more the child will experience problems in the future.
the more children are insecure, and the more they inhibit their behavior in order to obtain security, the more problems they have in school.
the more children are inhibited, the more they seek security from their teachers, the more problems they have.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
emotional security seeking is a key factor in the adaptation process of young children after entry to kindergarten.
children adapt to their new school environment by trying to establish emotional security, and that the extent of this adaptation is related to the extent of emotional security.
children's adaptation after entry to school is characterized by the development of a secure relationship with the teacher, and by a decrease in behavioral inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
teachers should pay more attention to the emotional security of their students, especially in the beginning of school.
children's behavior in the classroom is related to their feelings and that their behavior in the classroom can help teachers understand how they are feeling.
the first few weeks of school are a critical time for children to feel secure in school.
